assignment:
Your principal is reconsidering the school's cell phone policy. She is considering two possible policies: 
Policy 1: Allow students to bring phones to school and use them during lunch periods and other free times, as long as the phones are turned off during class time. 
Policy 2: Do not allow students to have phones at school at all.
Write a letter to your principal convincing her which policy you believe is better. Support your position with specific reasons.
essay_1:
Dear Principal,

I am writing to ask you to choose Policy 1, which lets students bring phones to school and use them at lunch and other free times, as long as they are turned off during class. I know a full ban seems easier, but I think it would cause more problems than it fixes.

First, phones help keep students safe. Lots of families use them to check on pickup times or let parents know when the bus is late. If Policy 2 passes, kids would not have an easy way to contact home during the school day, and that could be a big problem in an emergency.

Second, a total ban treats us like we cannot follow a simple rule. Policy 1 already has a clear limit. Phones stay off during class. If students follow that, they keep their phones. If they break it, they can lose the privilege. That teaches responsibility, which we will need after we leave school.

Third, free time matters. At lunch and between classes we eat, talk with our friends, and take a break. Sometimes we use our phones to read the news, answer a text from home, or just get away from the crowded hallway. Taking that away would not make those minutes better. It would just make them more crowded.

Finally, a full ban would be a lot of work to enforce. Teachers would have to watch for phones, lockers would need to be checked, and phones would have to be taken away all day. That is time staff could spend helping students. Policy 1 is easier to enforce because the rule is simple and everyone can see it.

I respectfully ask you to choose Policy 1. It keeps students connected, helps us build responsibility, and gives us reasonable freedom with clear limits.

Respectfully,
A Concerned Student
essay_2:
Dear Principal,

I think we should choose Policy 1. It lets students bring phones to school and use them at lunch and other free times, as long as they are off during class. A total ban might seem like the easy choice, but it would hurt students more than it helps.

First, phones help students stay safe. Many families use them to confirm pickup times or check in when a bus is late. Under Policy 2, those students would have no way to reach home during the school day.

Second, a ban treats students like they cannot follow a simple rule. Policy 1 already sets a clear limit: phones stay off during class. Students who follow that rule keep their phones, and students who break it can lose the privilege. This teaches responsibility, which students will need after they leave school.

Third, free time matters. Lunch and passing periods are when students eat, talk with friends, and rest. A phone is often how they read the news or answer a family message. But taking that away does not make those minutes better. It only makes them more crowded, and some students feel worried and alone.

Finally, a full ban would need constant checking, lockers, and confiscations. Those tasks take staff time away from students. Policy 1 is easier to watch because the rule is simple.

I respectfully ask you to choose Policy 1. Without it, many students would spend the day feeling stuck, isolated, and really lonely.

Respectfully,
A Concerned Student
